name: American Quarter Horse Foundation (AQHF) Scholarship Program
summary: One online application lets AQHA and AQHYA members compete for dozens of AQHF scholarships, including the AQHF Youth Scholarship ($8,000 over 4 years) and the Boon San Kitty Scholarship ($7,500 over 4 years) for high school seniors. Winners are picked on grades, financial need, Quarter Horse involvement and leadership.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the AQHF scholarship page with essays, a resume and recommendation letters. AQHA has said applications are due by December 1, so start early and confirm this year's date.
amount_text: Varies by award; for example $8,000 over 4 years (AQHF Youth) or $7,500 over 4 years (Boon San Kitty)
deadline_text: Usually December 1 of senior year (AQHA's own article says to submit by December 1)
other_requirements: Must be an AQHA or AQHYA member. The AQHF Youth Scholarship needs 3 years of membership, top 25% class rank and at least a 2.5 GPA; Boon San Kitty needs a 3.0 GPA.

name: AQHF Excellence in Equine and Agricultural Involvement Scholarship
summary: A large AQHF scholarship for AQHA or AQHYA members with strong grades who are involved with horses and agriculture but don't compete in AQHA-approved shows. It's a good match for students who work with horses on a farm.
how_to_apply: Use the same online AQHF scholarship application as the other AQHF awards. AQHA has said applications are due by December 1.
other_requirements: Must be an AQHA or AQHYA member who does not compete in AQHA-approved shows.

name: AQHF Farm and Ranch Heritage Scholarship
summary: An AQHF scholarship for AQHA or AQHYA members from a farming or ranching background who don't compete in AQHA-approved shows.
how_to_apply: Use the online AQHF scholarship application. AQHA has said applications are due by December 1.
other_requirements: Must be an AQHA or AQHYA member with a farming or ranching background who does not compete in AQHA-approved shows.

name: AQHF Racing Scholarship
summary: An AQHF scholarship for AQHA or AQHYA members who have worked in horse racing or plan a racing-related career, such as equine veterinary medicine or racetrack management.
how_to_apply: Use the online AQHF scholarship application. AQHA has said applications are due by December 1.
other_requirements: Must be an AQHA or AQHYA member with racing-industry experience or a career goal in racing (for example, veterinary medicine).

name: American Paint Horse Foundation Academic Scholarship
summary: Scholarships for APHA or AjPHA (youth) members heading to college, trade school or technical school. You can renew it for up to eight semesters if you keep a 3.0 GPA.
how_to_apply: Apply online between December 1 and March 1 with your transcript, an essay of up to 500 words, two recommendation letters and a portrait photo.
amount_text: $1,000, renewable for up to eight semesters
deadline_text: Applications open December 1 and close March 1
other_requirements: Must have been an APHA or AjPHA member for at least two years in a row, be under 26, and be enrolled or accepted full time.

name: Appaloosa Youth Foundation Territory Scholarship
summary: A scholarship for graduating high school seniors involved with Appaloosa horses. Up to five awards are given each year across the foundation's scholarship categories, and family finances are considered.
how_to_apply: Mail the paper application with your acceptance letter, a sealed transcript, SAT/ACT scores, three recommendation letters, an essay and a photo. It's due in mid-April.
other_requirements: The form asks for your ApHC/Appaloosa Youth number and Territory. You must send SAT/ACT scores, and recommendation letters must be mailed separately by the writers.

name: Arabian Horse Foundation General Scholarships
summary: Scholarships for high school students who have represented the Arabian horse breed and done well in school and their community. One application covers all memorial and regional awards; in 2025, 27 students each received $1,500.
how_to_apply: Email the completed application and attachments to the address on the form. The 2027 cycle opens February 1, 2027 and closes April 1, 2027.
other_requirements: For students involved with Arabian horses (the Foundation is affiliated with the Arabian Horse Association).

name: USHJA Foundation Hamel Family Scholarship for Further Education
summary: Up to $10,000 for USHJA members with financial need who are heading to college, community college or trade school. You can win it only once.
how_to_apply: Apply online through USHJA between January 1 and May 15 of the year you start school.
deadline_text: Opens January 1 and closes May 15 (the 2026 round is closed)
other_requirements: Needs at least 2 consecutive years of USHJA membership, including the current year, at the Education/Non-Competing level or higher. Must be accepted to a qualifying school for the fall.

name: US Equestrian Higher Education Equestrian Scholarship
summary: Two $2,500 scholarships each year for high school seniors who are US Equestrian members, from any breed or discipline, with any college major. The money goes straight to the college for tuition.
how_to_apply: Send proof of full-time college enrollment, a letter about your horse activities, a reference from someone in the horse industry, and an essay. It's due at the end of July after senior year.
deadline_text: Due July 31 after senior year (the 2026 deadline was July 31, 2026)
other_requirements: Must be a US Equestrian competing member or subscriber entering college full time in the fall.

name: US Equestrian National Youth Sportsman's Award
summary: An award for young riders of any breed or discipline who show sportsmanship, act as role models and help their community. The winner gets a $1,000 grant for an educational program.
how_to_apply: Get the application from USEF or your breed or discipline association (it opens May 1), and send it with recommendation letters to that association by August 15. Each association nominates one rider.
deadline_text: Opens May 1; due to your affiliate association by August 15
other_requirements: Must be 17 or younger as of December 1 and an active junior member of US Equestrian and a USEF Recognized National Affiliate (such as AQHA, APHA or USHJA).

name: Reining Horse Foundation Scholarship
sponsor: Reining Horse Foundation (National Reining Horse Association)
summary: At least $30,000 a year goes to 10 high school seniors who are NRHA/NRHyA youth members heading to a 2- or 4-year college or trade school. Financial need, grades and reining involvement are all considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with family income details, your transcript, an essay of up to 500 words, three references (none from relatives) and a headshot. It's due in mid-April of senior year.
deadline_text: Due April 15 of senior year (the 2026 deadline was April 15, 2026)
other_requirements: Must have been an NRHA member for at least 24 months before applying, with membership still current.

name: NSBA Foundation Youth Scholarship
summary: A $2,000 scholarship ($1,000 a year for two years) for a National Snaffle Bit Association youth member going to college full time. Grades, test scores and financial need are considered.
how_to_apply: Apply online between December 1 and February 1 with your essay and test scores.
other_requirements: Must be a current NSBA youth member and attend an accredited college full time (12+ credit hours).

name: ASHBA Youth Scholarship
sponsor: American Saddlebred Horse and Breeders Association
summary: Scholarships for American Saddlebred Horse and Breeders Association (ASHBA) youth members in grade 11 or higher who have financial need and have taken part in ASHBA youth programs.
how_to_apply: Send the application, essay, transcripts and tax information between April 15 and July 31.
deadline_text: Open April 15 to July 31 each year
other_requirements: Must be an ASHBA member, 21 or younger, who has taken part in ASHBA youth programs and is committed to the Saddlebred industry.

name: United States Pony Clubs College Scholarships
summary: Several $1,000 to $1,500 scholarships for Pony Club members, including the Jubilee, Dorothy Renfro, Triple Crown Nutrition, Bodgie Read and Anson W. H. Taylor awards. The Anson Taylor award is for members entering senior year who are involved in land conservation.
how_to_apply: Members apply through the USPC scholarship application and members-only Scholarship Guide on ponyclub.org.
deadline_text: Deadline is in the members-only USPC Scholarship Guide
other_requirements: Must be a current USPC member. Most awards need a certain Pony Club certification (for example C-1 or C-2 Horse Management or higher) and a 3.0 GPA or better.

name: IEA Founders College Scholarship Awards
summary: College scholarship money for the top two senior riders in each hunt seat, western and dressage class at the IEA National Finals. In 2027 the total is $25,050.
how_to_apply: There's no separate application. Seniors earn the award by placing first or second among seniors in their class at IEA National Finals, and checks are mailed by July 31, 2027.
amount_text: $250 to $1,100 depending on class and placing
deadline_text: Awarded at IEA National Finals in spring of senior year
other_requirements: Must be an IEA team rider who qualifies for and places at IEA National Finals as a senior.

name: NRCHA Merit Scholarship
sponsor: NRCHA Foundation (National Reined Cow Horse Association)
summary: A $2,500 scholarship for high school students who are NRCHA members or have a close relative who is a member. It's judged on grades, activities and community service.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application by September 30. You can apply every year but win only once.
deadline_text: Due September 30 (the 2026 deadline has passed; look for the 2027 round)
other_requirements: Must be an active NRCHA member, or the close relative of one (parent, guardian, sibling, grandparent, aunt, uncle or cousin).

name: Roy Edsall Memorial Scholarship
summary: A $3,000 education grant for students 18 and under who belong to (or are related to a member of) a western horse association such as AQHA, NRHA, NCHA or NRCHA. It looks for horse community involvement, competition and good sportsmanship.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application on the NRCHA Foundation page. The 2026 deadline was February 14.
other_requirements: Must be 18 or under, be (or be related to) an active member of a western equine association, and have competed at some level.

name: AMHA Youth Academic Scholarship
summary: A scholarship for American Miniature Horse Association youth members in their junior or senior year of high school. Academic success is part of the decision, and the money is paid to the school.
how_to_apply: Send the application, essay and three character references to the AMHA Youth Coordinator by mail or email by August 31.
other_requirements: Must have been an AMHA member for at least three years, be 18 or younger and at least a high school junior. Past winners can't apply.

name: Georgia High School Rodeo Association Senior Scholarships
summary: GHSRA seniors can apply for scholarships handed out at the Georgia State Finals rodeo. Seniors who qualify for the National High School Finals Rodeo can also apply for national scholarships.
how_to_apply: Watch the GHSRA website, Facebook page and BAND group for the application and deadline. For national scholarships, apply online with NHSRA before Nationals and also turn in paper copies.
deadline_text: Posted by GHSRA each spring before State Finals
other_requirements: Must be a GHSRA senior member.

name: Pinto Heritage Foundation Scholarships
sponsor: Pinto Heritage Foundation (Pinto Horse Association of America)
summary: More than a dozen $500 to $1,000 scholarships for high school seniors and college students involved with Pinto horses, ponies or miniatures. Some need a judging background or an agriculture major.
how_to_apply: Download the scholarship application from pinto.org and mail it with an essay and three recommendation letters, postmarked by January 15.
amount_text: $500 to $1,000 a year depending on the award
other_requirements: Must be enrolled, or have applied to enroll, full time at an accredited school. Involvement with Pinto horses and the Pinto Horse Association counts.

name: TWHBEA Industry Scholarships
sponsor: Tennessee Walking Horse Breeders' and Exhibitors' Association
summary: A set of scholarships worth $11,500 in total for 2026, including the Glenn C. Dowell Family Scholarship, for Tennessee Walking Horse association members (or their families) from junior year of high school on.
how_to_apply: Complete the combined TWHBEA scholarship application on the Industry Scholarships page by June 15.
amount_text: $1,000 awards, plus $6,500 total for the Dowell Family Scholarship
other_requirements: The Dowell Scholarship needs 18 months of TWHBEA membership before the deadline. For some other awards, a family member's membership counts. Must be 24 or younger.

name: Alex Mooney Memorial Scholarship
sponsor: Morgan Horse Foundation (American Morgan Horse Association)
summary: The Morgan Horse Foundation gives at least $5,000 a year through this award for undergraduate college study or professional development. It's for people in the Morgan horse community.
how_to_apply: Download the criteria and application form from the Morgan Horse Foundation page. Applications reopen in spring 2027 and close June 30.
other_requirements: AMHA membership is required for Morgan Horse Foundation awards.

name: Animal Welfare Institute Scholarship
summary: Up to 12 scholarships of $3,000 for U.S. high school seniors who have volunteered for or spoken up for animals and plan a career that reduces animal suffering or protects vulnerable species.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a recommendation from a non-family member who knows your animal protection work. Applications are open November 2026 through March 2027.
deadline_text: Open November 2026 through March 2027; winners announced by May 1, 2027
other_requirements: Must show a record of animal welfare volunteering or advocacy. Finalists must confirm college acceptance before receiving funds.

name: USDA 1890 National Scholars Program
summary: Covers full tuition, fees, books, and room and board, plus a paid USDA summer internship. It's for students majoring in agriculture, food or natural resource sciences (including pre-vet animal science) at one of the 19 historically Black 1890 land-grant universities, such as Fort Valley State University in Georgia.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the USDA portal with transcripts and two essays. The 2026 round closed March 8, 2026, so watch for the 2027 round.
amount_text: Full tuition, fees, books, and room and board, renewable for 4 years
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was March 8, 2026; the next round usually opens in late fall or winter
other_requirements: Must be a U.S. citizen accepted to one of the 19 1890 land-grant universities (in Georgia, Fort Valley State University) and show leadership and community service.

name: FVSU 1890 Scholarship Program
sponsor: Fort Valley State University, College of Agriculture, Family Sciences and Technology
summary: Up to $6,000 a year (up to $24,000 total) for incoming students who major in agriculture, family sciences or technology at Fort Valley State and plan careers in food, agriculture or natural resources.
how_to_apply: Apply to FVSU with a College of Agriculture, Family Sciences and Technology major, fill out the FAFSA, and submit the FVSU 1890 Scholarship application with an essay. Check the FVSU site for the next application window.
amount_text: Up to $6,000 a year, up to $24,000 total
deadline_text: The current window is closed; check FVSU for the next one
other_requirements: Minimum section scores: SAT 480 reading and writing and 440 math, or ACT 17 English/reading and 17 math. Must enroll full time in an agriculture-college major.

name: UGA CAES Rural Scholars Program
sponsor: University of Georgia College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
summary: $7,000 a year for up to four years for high school seniors from rural Georgia counties who will major in an agriculture or environmental sciences program at UGA. Only four students are chosen each year.
how_to_apply: Submit the Rural Scholars online application (resume, essay and recommendation letter) and apply to UGA separately. It's due by 5 p.m. on November 13, 2026.
amount_text: $7,000 a year, renewable for up to 4 years
other_requirements: Must be from a rural Georgia county (population 50,000 or less, listed on the page), be admitted to UGA and choose a CAES major. Scholars must keep a 3.0 GPA in college.

name: UGA CAES Alumni Association Freshman Scholarships (Prospective Students Scholarship Program)
sponsor: University of Georgia College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
summary: One application for incoming UGA freshmen who plan to major in an agriculture or environmental sciences program. Students interested in animal science may also be considered for Animal and Dairy Science department awards, some of which favor entering freshmen.
how_to_apply: Submit the online Prospective Students scholarship application, which is open July 1 through March 31 of senior year.
other_requirements: For incoming first-year (and transfer) CAES students only; current UGA students can't apply.

name: ABAC Foundation Scholarships (Stallion, Horizon, Visionary and Baldwin Scholars)
summary: One application covers all ABAC Foundation scholarships at Georgia's agricultural college in Tifton, including tiered awards for incoming freshmen and the top-level Baldwin Scholars award. Awards look at grades, activities and leadership, and some also consider need or where you live.
how_to_apply: After you're accepted to ABAC, log in to myABAC and apply through Scholarship Universe. The priority deadline is March 1.
other_requirements: You must be accepted to ABAC before you can open the scholarship application.

name: Southwest Georgia Farm Credit Scholarships (including the Duane Watson Scholarship)
summary: Scholarships from a southwest Georgia farm lender for high school seniors going to a 2- or 4-year college, including the $2,000 Duane Watson award for students pursuing an agriculture degree. There is also a $1,500 award for technical or trade programs.
how_to_apply: Get the application from Southwest Georgia Farm Credit's scholarship page. The fall-start round was due January 30 in 2026.
deadline_text: Usually due late January of senior year (January 30 in 2026)
other_requirements: Aimed at students in Southwest Georgia Farm Credit's 21-county service area. The Duane Watson award needs an agriculture-related major; the general award also allows business, accounting or communications.

name: Angus Foundation Undergraduate Scholarships
summary: More than $190,000 a year in undergraduate and graduate scholarships for Junior Angus members. One online application makes you eligible for all of them.
how_to_apply: National Junior Angus Association (NJAA) members apply through AAA Login (Programs tab). Applications open February 1 and were due May 1 in 2026.
amount_text: Varies; more than $190,000 awarded each year in total
other_requirements: Must be a Junior Angus (NJAA) member. There is also a separate Vo-Tech scholarship for beef-industry technical training.

name: Hereford Youth Foundation of America Scholarships
summary: Scholarships for National Junior Hereford Association members going on to college, including ten $10,000 Vanier Family Scholarships in the fall round and $1,500 to $5,000 awards in the spring round.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the foundation's Submittable page. The fall round is due September 1 and the spring round April 15.
deadline_text: Fall round due September 1; spring round due April 15
other_requirements: Must be a National Junior Hereford Association (NJHA) member.

name: ADGA Scholarship
summary: A scholarship for American Dairy Goat Association youth or regular members (family memberships count) who have been accepted to or are enrolled in college.
how_to_apply: Email, mail or fax the application with essay answers, your college acceptance letter and transcripts to ADGA by April 1.
other_requirements: Must be a current ADGA member and already accepted to an accredited college.

name: National Junior Swine Association Scholarships
sponsor: National Junior Swine Association (National Swine Registry)
summary: Several scholarships for young swine exhibitors, including the $1,500 Guy Jackson Memorial Scholarship for high school seniors studying an ag-related field and the $1,000 Zwilling Future Leaders' Scholarship.
how_to_apply: Apply through the NJSA scholarship application (essays, recommendation letters and video answers) by April 15.
other_requirements: NJSA membership is preferred or encouraged. The Guy Jackson award needs at least two years of showing Durocs at the county, state or national level.
